For Petitioner: Mr. R.Sethuvarayar  For Respondents: Mr.Abishek Murthy, Governme  for R1, R3 & R4  ORDER
The petitioner seeks a direction for the consideration of the representation dated 22.09.2023 for re-conveyance under Section 48B of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (the 1894 Act).

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the lands earlier owned by the petitioner were acquired under the 1894 Act for purposes for constructing staff quarters for employees of the Ennore Port Trust.
He submits further that the lands were not used for the said purpose and that the petitioner is still in occupation thereof.

3 . M r . A b i s h e k M u r t h y , l e a r n e d A d d i t i o n a l G o v e r n m e n t P l e a d e r , a c c e p t s https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 04/12/2025 07:51:23 pm ) notice for all the respondents.

By referring to the judgment of the Honble Supreme Court in Indore Development Authority v. Manoharlal & others, (2020) 8 SCC 129, he submits that Section 101 of Act 30 of 2013 is not applicable to an acquisition under the 1894 Act.

entities.text: Indore Development Authority v. Manoharlal & others, (2020) 8 SCC 129
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, he submits that the relief claimed by the petitioner cannot be countenanced.
4. On perusal of the affidavit in support of the writ petition, it is evident that the award was issued in 1999 and 2003.
It is also clear that compensation was deposited in the Treasury.
The present writ petition has been filed more than two decades later.

In these circumstances, the request of the petitioner cannot be countenanced especially in view of the inapplicability of Section 101 of Act 30 of 2013 to proceedings under the 1894 Act, and the repeal of the 1894 Act.
5. Therefore, the writ petition stands dismissed without any order as to costs.
